instruction: Sort the data in the spreadsheet by the Quantity column in descending order (highest to lowest).

metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting data by Quantity column in descending order. Verified with Python that after sorting, top 3 quantities are: 124 (Quad), 93 (Fire Aspen), 91 (Aspen). Evaluator checks cells E2, E3, E4 contain these values.

llm_judge_reasons: CRITICAL: Incomplete coverage - evaluator only checks 3 cells (E2, E3, E4) but does not verify the ENTIRE Quantity column is sorted in descending order
CRITICAL: For a 28-row dataset, checking only top 3 values cannot confirm all data is sorted correctly - rows 5-28 could be in wrong order
CRITICAL: Evaluator would pass even if an agent manually sets E2=124, E3=93, E4=91 without actually performing a sort operation
CRITICAL: No verification that the sort operation affected all rows - partial sorts or manual reordering would incorrectly pass
The instruction requires sorting the ENTIRE dataset, but the evaluator only verifies a small subset of the result
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Check ALL cells in column E (E2 through E29 for 28 data rows) to ensure complete descending order, not just the top 3
Add rules to verify E2>=E3>=E4>=E5...>=E29 for the entire dataset
Alternatively, use sheet_data comparison against a fully sorted expected file to verify the complete sort operation
Current approach only validates 10.7% of the data (3 out of 28 rows), which is semantically insufficient for verifying a sort instruction
